vintage: INE Censo anual de población (Ocupación y actividad), 1 January 2024

rule.text: A district appears when the city's employed residents in its CNAE divisions are at least 1.25 times the national share and number at least 1,000 or 1% of the city's employed residents, or when one of its listed specialities is at least 3 times the national share with at least 5,000 people or 0.5% of the city's employed. Districts are ranked by how many people they employ above the national norm; up to 5 per city. A Harbor also needs a city hex on or next to water or a mapped river. The city type is named after the strongest district, or after a listed district with a quotient of at least 6 and at least 3% of the city's employed when there is one; 'Capital city' goes to Madrid's Government plaza. Employment is the INE Annual Population Census (employed residents, counted where they live, by two-digit CNAE-2009 division) for the 151 cities INE publishes at that detail.
rule.county_note: Municipalities have no districts of their own: the census publishes two-digit divisions only for the main cities.

method.note: The census counts employed residents where they live, by the CNAE-2009 division of their job; it has no wages, so there is no average pay. Two-digit divisions are coarser than US NAICS codes.
